text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.
- Parliament enacted legislation to return property nationalised during the 1945-90 Yugoslav communist era to former owners or provide them alternative compensation.
- Banks could soon offer favourable mortgages - a law that should enable citizens to get a loan to buy a flat without previously having to deposit a third of the sum could be passed next year.
- Stocks: textile firm Varteks recorded a 145 percent growth on Croatia's over-the counter market.
- Prices of most, and especially food products will go up after January 1, due to value added tax. Finance Minister Bozo Prka has therefore announced 8-10 percent rise of net salaries.
- Croatian Airlines has to renew its fleet by the year 2002, as its noisy planes will no longer be allowed to land at European airports.
- In 1996 Croatia bought four ships for its merchant navy.
- Some 600 American IFOR troops have already pulled out of northern Bosnia via Croatia.
- Some 138,881 foreign tourists visited Zagreb in the first eight months of 1996, most of which were Americans. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
